subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The First Automobile
description: Learn The First Automobile in one minute.

hook.text: In 1886, Karl Benz built a three-wheeled machine that most people called a useless toy.

buildup.text: He had spent years shrinking a gasoline engine small enough to sit on a carriage frame.

discovery.text: His Patent-Motorwagen became the first true car—a vehicle driven by an internal engine.

twist.text: Almost nobody bought one. People trusted horses far more than loud, smelly machines.

climax.text: Then Bertha Benz secretly drove it 65 miles to prove it worked—the first road trip ever.

punchline.text: One bold drive changed how the world saw cars.

quiz.question: Who made the first long-distance car trip?

details.summary: Karl Benz built and patented the first true automobile in 1886, a three-wheeled vehicle powered by a gasoline internal combustion engine, in Mannheim, Germany.
details.whyItMatters: The Benz Patent-Motorwagen is recognized as the birth of the automobile as we know it, launching an industry that would reshape cities, economies, and daily life worldwide.
takeaways: Benz received Patent No. 37435 for his motorwagen in 1886
It had a single-cylinder engine producing about two-thirds of a horsepower
His wife Bertha made the first long-distance car trip in 1888

faq.question: Is Karl Benz the sole inventor of the automobile?
faq.answer: Several inventors contributed, but Benz is credited with the first practical, purpose-built motorcar. Gottlieb Daimler independently developed a gasoline engine around the same time in a nearby city.

faq.question: How far could the first automobile travel?
faq.answer: The Motorwagen had very limited range. Bertha Benz's famous 1888 trip covered about 65 miles and required fuel purchased from pharmacies, as gas stations did not yet exist.
